method: Static facts, complete native entry-path disassembly, bounded arithmetic-only unpacking, restricted CIL interpretation, source/API trace and dependency fetch/signature review. No sample application or downloaded installer was executed.

samples.name: emulator
samples.marker: Inert PE stub: invalid IAT call; no reachable harmful behavior
samples.identification: Malformed, inert native PE; likely constructed analysis/test stub, no verified vendor identity
execution_evidence: ImageBase 0x400000; entry 0x401000 contains FF 15 64 21 00 00 / 31 C0 / C3. The indirect call reads absolute address 0x2164, whereas the IsDebuggerPresent IAT slot is at 0x402164. Under ordinary image mapping this faults before reaching xor eax,eax/ret.

The remaining 503 bytes of the only executable section are zero. No TLS callbacks, relocations, resources, decoder, alternate entry, or reachable network/process-memory operation were found. Imports include memory/thread/hard-error/process/debug APIs but are unused by the reachable code.

A roughly four-megabyte nonexecutable .junk section overlaps part of the import bytes and has near-random entropy; a 1024-byte overlay is also opaque. There is no code path that reads, decodes or executes either region. No URLs/dependencies were recovered from facts or raw strings.
samples.judgment_basis: The complete reachable code is inert/malformed; alarming imports and padded entropy explain a suspicious static profile without establishing harmful behavior. A legitimate product identity and original deployment circumstances are missing. The inaccessible sandbox report cannot explain its score.

samples.name: loader
samples.marker: RC Tool Drivers: user-selected driver and runtime installation
samples.identification: RC Tool Drivers 1.0.0.0, native .NET Reactor wrapper around a Windows Forms driver/runtime installer
execution_evidence: Native CRT entry 0x40cd2f reaches main/protector 0x4019f0. Resource RT_RCDATA/__ at RVA 0x2a3d0 is 4,145,226 bytes. Bounded x86 arithmetic emulation of 0x401300 produces substitution tables; 0x401560 applies forward/reverse adjacent-byte lookup feedback to 1024-byte blocks.

Reproduced decoding yields size 4,514,830 followed by a checksum-valid zlib stream. Decompression recovers v4.0.30319 plus a 14-byte prefix and a 4,514,816-byte managed bootstrap DLL, SHA256 d67a3b5498f1762fefcf04843197648dfe8a4047f6d40639324b3c72872cb329.

The native CLRCreateInstance/metahost/runtime/AppDomain path loads the bootstrap. Managed method ___ reads resource _, calls Assembly.Load, obtains EntryPoint, and invokes it with command-line arguments. The inner assembly is 4,508,672 bytes, SHA256 4742655862c9fc390cf3f7aeda92163b02d5efc7226ed509d60bcece41df15ae.

A restricted CIL data interpreter selects the resource-decoding subgraph of method 388 (LDFgNmI4H, RVA 0x17970), without invoking the program, OS, network, or native imports. It decrypts 7,760 bytes; a verified ldind.i8/xor/stind.i8 loop uses 83,539,615. The stream contains 303 prefix/header patch records, restored with bounds checks to their PE RVAs.

Pure interpretation of method 381 (JOwBkxj9q, RVA 0x143cc) recovers the complete 20,846-byte UTF-16 string table: 299 records. All records parse to the exact end. Method 380 checks Debugger.IsAttached and throws Debugger Detected: protector anti-debugging, not evidence of payload theft.

Restored Main (method 256) initializes Windows Forms and runs Form1 (constructor 58). User selection handlers construct driver/runtime lists. Async download state machines (including method 101) use GetTempPath/Path.Combine and WebClient.DownloadFileTaskAsync with progress and cancellation callbacks.

Installation paths require the staged file to exist, populate ProcessStartInfo.FileName with that file, use the runas verb, choose installer-specific quiet/passive/norestart arguments, start the process and wait for exit. DirectX extraction invokes dxsetup.exe and cleans DX_Temp_Files. Driver removal uses pnputil.exe /enum-drivers then /delete-driver <selected .inf> /uninstall /force for listed phone-driver vendors. No UAC exploit, hidden remote tasking, credential acquisition, persistence or exfiltration was established.

All 25 decrypted Google Drive references were fetched with forager and provenance retained in scratch. They are 10 ChimeraTool phone-driver installers and 15 Microsoft runtime/DirectX/.NET installers. Every Authenticode content digest matches; osslsigncode fully verifies 10 vendor installers, while 15 Microsoft packages encounter legacy trust-chain/timestamp validation limits. The current downloaded bytes, version metadata and signatures support the disclosed installation role.
samples.judgment_basis: Recovered UI, selection-to-download-to-install execution paths and current publisher-signed dependencies support a legitimate driver installer. The unsigned wrapper, custom resource concealment, protector anti-debugging and requested administrator rights merit scrutiny but do not establish malicious intent. Publisher authorization to redistribute every package and the machine deployment context are unknown. Collector malware-family names are not supported attribution.
samples.stage_detection_correction: Saving the inner assembly as analyst-chosen .bin activated an unsupported hostile filename/structure profile. Identical bytes restored/saved as .exe did not. The property profile is now notable metadata; its registry-reference consumer is now a notable capability. The raw wrapper retains its original suspicious custom resource-concealment finding.

samples.name: circuit
samples.marker: CircuitPython HID demo: known fixture; retain suspicious bypass
samples.identification: CircuitPython HID regression fixture expressing an NVISO Digispark demonstration technique
execution_evidence: Constructs Keyboard(usb_hid.devices), waits two seconds, sends GUI+R, waits 0.5 seconds, and calls KeyboardLayoutUS.write with hidden policy-bypassing PowerShell DownloadString/Invoke-Expression text ending in LF.

Fetched official Adafruit keyboard, keycode, layout-base and US-layout sources. Keyboard.send presses then releases HID reports; layout.write maps characters to keycodes. US layout maps LF to HID Return (0x28), so the command submits. No CR-only or file-write behavior is inferred.

SHA256 exactly matches testdata/hid-command-injection/circuitpython-newline.py, a documented inert regression source fixture based on the NVISO public demonstration. The primary article describes a test device and harmless demonstration payloads. The selected URL is a placeholder; forager failed DNS resolution for updates.example.net/stage.ps1. No second stage was recovered or assumed.

No source obfuscation, stolen data, persistence, destructive action or further hidden stage exists in the supplied source. Actual target authorization and installed CircuitPython/library versions are not provided. Upstream current sources validate API semantics, not a specific deployed dependency version.
samples.judgment_basis: The exact regression-fixture provenance, documented educational source and placeholder destination tip this artifact to BENIGN. HID command submission and hidden execution-policy bypass remain accurate notable/suspicious observations and would warrant investigation on an unexplained deployed device.

rule_changes: Retained all supported findings on the three originals. Eight original matcher/scope/criticality sets were preserved during relocation or renaming; see moves map. NtOpenProcess no longer claims syscall setup; NtReadVirtualMemory is a memory-read reference; resource entropy belongs to resource entropy; DOS-prefix bytes do not establish embedded PE images or multiple images; executable URL literals are URL-path evidence; relative-route fetch is an HTTP client operation; a PNG/metadata resource profile does not establish a UI bundle.

HID hidden-policy-bypass composite remains matched but changes hostile to suspicious because the required behavior also occurs in the published authorized demonstration and exact repository fixture. All 33 existing positive and near-miss cases pass unchanged.

The inner managed assembly saved under an analyst-chosen .bin suffix demonstrated that the unsigned DLL data-extension profile does not prove malicious disguise, packing, random exports, or an execution technique. Moved it to notable extension/structure metadata and moved its Run/rename API-reference consumer to a notable registry capability. No primitive was removed.

Updated exact consumers. A newly redundant version-resource downgrade leg was removed because the existing resource directory already covers it. Two resource-carrier suppressors now select measured resource-size context rather than a directory covering their own newly relocated required DOS-prefix leg. Focused real attack-fixture comparison found no lost findings.

Broad resource-namespace suppressors were audited: the relocated near-random resource requires a section >=262144 bytes (already covered by pre-existing resource-size evidence); DOS-prefix PEs are covered by pre-existing resource inventory/icon-count observations in the exercised original and attack controls. Their generic metadata context was not duplicated to tune a classifier.

verification.attack_fixture_comparison: No findings lost or gained after normalizing relocated IDs; hostile/suspicious counts retained, including archive members.
verification.renaming_control: Fabricated Wintun OSD attack fixture retained both hostile identities under both .dat and .dll names; all embedded members were compared.
verification.yaml_parse: All changed/new YAML files parse; git diff --check is clean.
verification.final_required_command: make validate; result recorded by final command output
verification.fixture_id_maintenance: Updated same-origin collect POST fixture assertion to the relocated relative-route fetch ID after validation exposed the stale expectation. The fixture behavior and expected criticality remain unchanged.

remaining_rule_classifier_disagreements: For the three original files, calibrated ML classes remain 0 and level -1 before/after. Their BENIGN verdicts do not imply clearing the retained suspicious protector/HID findings. Raw model probabilities remain high (listed per sample); the v18 model warns that the extractor feature schema is newer (expected v21).

Supplementary fetched Microsoft installers expose out-of-batch shared-rule false positives: CAB/.NET/PNG/dynamic-linking co-occurrence rules, an incomplete legacy Microsoft issuing-CA pin set, and ADISPLAY mis-extracted across a pointer followed by the wide DISPLAY string in the VC++ 2013 bootstrapper. Dependency signatures, image digests, member layouts and application purpose refute malware attribution from these findings. These downstream rule families were recorded as remaining disagreements rather than used to label RC Tool Drivers malicious.
limitations: Supplied tria.ge pages were inaccessible; external scores were treated only as leads.
Google Drive references are mutable; the fetched bytes support this review date, not a guarantee about future responses.
The recovered protected assembly requires runtime self-patching in normal execution; recovery here reconstructed static data and paths without running the application.
